Geometry checks & planning notes

    Exterior classification is geometric, not semantic. It excludes nested contours, which may include lattice or important cavities. SLC uses midpoint section geometry and minimum-Z records. Verify a sample in your internal printer reader before a production run.

    Layer schedule

    Consecutive layers with the same thickness and rule are grouped below. Click a row to select its height range.

    Z range · mmThicknessLayersRule

    A deliberate layer plan.

    1. Load and arrange. Drop one or more watertight STL files. Confirm units and bed size. Scan checks the mesh and arranges parts without changing their upright orientation.
    2. Choose where to move faster. The baseline is 100 µm. Vertical exterior walls and the support region use your preferred thickness, initially 150 µm. Sloped exterior sections retain the baseline.
    3. Override with intent. Set a height range or drag the right-hand rail, then add a 50–200 µm band. Manual bands take priority over support and automatic rules. Boundaries snap to 0.05 mm.
    4. Calibrate the estimate. Add resin Ec, Dp and measured irradiance. Enter your non-exposure cycle time. The curve predicts exposure duration, not surface roughness.
    5. Export and verify. Download the SLC and companion recipe. Contours are sampled at layer midpoints. SLC stores minimum Z and up to 255 thickness runs. Import a representative result into your printer reader to verify compatibility.

    The support zone marks existing geometry; this app does not create supports. Internal nested contours are excluded from exterior slope decisions. Automatic cleanup reports welded vertices and removed degenerate or duplicate triangles. It is bounded: unresolved openings, intersections, or winding issues still require repair. Numerical sampling-plane adjustments are reported with the export. Profiles are browser-local; shared links do not include models or profiles.
